# Zoom Requirements Quality Checklist: Camera zoom targets

**Purpose**: Gate the requirements in spec 037 before `/speckit-tasks` — testing whether they are written well enough to build from, not whether any implementation works
**Created**: 2026-08-18
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**On deferred numbers**: 037 deliberately leaves the pixel band, the minimum tile
count and the ceiling to a dialling session. A deferred value is **not** a defect
here. Items below ask whether each deferral carries a rationale, a starting
point and a way to judge it — a spec that defers a number and says how it will
be settled is complete; one that simply omits it is not.

## Amendment Surface — does 037 supersede 036 cleanly?

- [ ] CHK001 Does the spec enumerate which of 036's requirements SURVIVE, rather than relying on a blanket "everything else stands"? 036 carries 28 functional requirements and the header names seven. [Completeness, Spec §Header]
- [ ] CHK002 Is 036's FR-004 still coherent once FR-003 is superseded? It reads "MUST NOT narrow below the **nominal** width", and "nominal" is the term FR-003 defined and 037 removes. [Conflict, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK003 Are 036's User Story 1 acceptance scenarios still valid? Scenario 2 turns on "below the nominal width" and scenario 3 on the camera holding "at the ceiling" as a multiple. [Conflict]
- [ ] CHK004 Does the spec state HOW the supersession is recorded — whether 036 is amended in place or left as shipped — so that someone reading 036 alone is not misled by a rule that no longer holds? [Gap, Traceability]
- [ ] CHK005 Are 036's remaining success criteria confirmed as still valid, given only SC-001 is named as superseded? [Completeness, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK006 Is 036's FR-005 behaviour (letting a wanderer leave rather than shrinking everyone) restated as preserved, given the requirement expressing it is the one being replaced? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK007 Does any 036 requirement outside the three named ones depend numerically on "10 tiles" or "1.5×"? [Gap, Conflict]
- [ ] CHK008 Is the relationship between 036's FR-029 (frame stays inside the world) and 037's FR-007 (ceiling narrower than the world) defined, given both constrain the frame against the world's edge? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007]

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK009 Are requirements defined for the case where the floor and ceiling tile counts meet or invert on a very small viewport? The data model acknowledges "they may meet; they may never invert" — the spec does not. [Gap]
- [ ] CHK010 Is the minimum tile count's interaction with the fine-detail threshold specified — that is, what governs when holding the minimum would push a tile below the threshold? [Gap, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK011 Are requirements defined for how often the floor and ceiling are recomputed, given the viewport can change at any time? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK012 Does the spec state whether the fit may sit anywhere between floor and ceiling, or only at the two limits? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK013 Are requirements specified for worlds smaller than the minimum tile count, where the minimum would exceed the world itself? [Coverage, Edge Case]

## Requirement Clarity & Measurability

- [ ] CHK014 Is "with margin" in FR-004 quantified, or left to the reader to infer from the 100/50 and 44 values? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK015 Can "a scene rather than a keyhole" be objectively evaluated, or is the minimum tile count the only operative definition? [Measurability, Spec §US2]
- [ ] CHK016 Is "roughly consistent" from the feature description reconciled with SC-001's explicit factor-of-2 bar? [Clarity, Consistency]
- [ ] CHK017 Is SC-008's "within 25%" justified, or is it an unexplained constant beside SC-004's "within 1%"? [Measurability, Spec §SC-008]
- [ ] CHK018 Is "the supported viewport range" defined once, with values, and referenced consistently rather than restated? [Clarity, Traceability]
- [ ] CHK019 Can FR-010's requirement to verify "across the full range of supported viewports" be satisfied objectively — is the sample of viewports enumerated or left open? [Measurability, Spec §FR-010]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK020 Do SC-004 and SC-008 scope their claims to the same population? SC-004 says "every viewport that reaches the pixel target"; SC-008 says "across the supported viewport range", which includes the clamped ones. [Conflict, Spec §SC-008]
- [ ] CHK021 Is the same term used throughout for the screen measurement — "viewport", "display", "map" — given the spec explicitly corrects the display/viewport confusion? [Consistency, Terminology]
- [ ] CHK022 Do FR-003 and SC-004 state the same claim about zoom range, and is one derived from the other rather than independently asserted? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK023 Is the Input section's description (ceiling as an absolute tile count) reconciled with the clarified decision, so it cannot be read as current intent? [Conflict, Spec §Input]
- [ ] CHK024 Are the clarification bullets consistent with the requirements they produced, with no decision recorded in one and contradicted in the other? [Consistency, Spec §Clarifications]

## Viewport Regime Coverage

- [ ] CHK025 Are requirements defined for all three regimes — target reachable, minimum binding, world clamping — or only for the regime where the target governs? [Coverage]
- [ ] CHK026 Is the boundary between regimes specified, so it is unambiguous which rule governs at the crossover? [Clarity, Gap]
- [ ] CHK027 Are the consequences of each regime stated as requirements rather than only as prose in the Overview table? [Traceability, Spec §Overview]
- [ ] CHK028 Are requirements defined for the `MAP_MAX_PX` cap regime, where a larger viewport produces no larger map? [Coverage, Gap]

## Degenerate Measurements & Resize

- [ ] CHK029 Are requirements defined for a viewport measurement of zero or undefined, which occurs before first layout and would make every formula in this feature divide by or multiply against it? [Gap, Edge Case]
- [ ] CHK030 Are requirements defined for a viewport small enough that the pixel band cannot be honoured at all — where the ceiling target exceeds the floor target in tiles? [Gap, Edge Case]
- [ ] CHK031 Does SC-009 cover resize across the world-clamp boundary as well as the minimum-tile boundary, or only the latter? [Coverage, Spec §SC-009]
- [ ] CHK032 Are requirements defined for a resize that occurs mid-transition, while the camera is already easing toward a target? [Gap, Coverage]
- [ ] CHK033 Are requirements defined for an orientation change, given the client has a documented short-viewport branch that fits width rather than height? [Gap, Coverage]
- [ ] CHK034 Is the behaviour on continuous resize specified as continuous, or only asserted to produce "no visible jump" at one boundary? [Clarity, Spec §SC-009]

## Deferred Decisions — is each deferral complete?

- [ ] CHK035 Does each deferred number carry a starting value, a rationale, and a stated way to judge it? [Completeness, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK036 Is it documented that the floor and ceiling targets cannot be dialled independently, since the zoom range is their ratio and moving one moves it? [Gap, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK037 Is the point at which deferral must end identified — which activity or gate requires the numbers to be settled? [Gap, Traceability]
- [ ] CHK038 Is the minimum tile count's trade documented, given it is the one deferred number with a genuine conflict behind it (framing against size and range)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK039 Is the Fog Generation dependency's effect on acceptance stated as a requirement, given SC-006 is expected to bind on today's world? [Consistency, Spec §Dependencies]
- [ ] CHK040 Is it unambiguous whether 037 may ship before Fog, and what is given up by doing so? [Clarity, Spec §Dependencies]
- [ ] CHK041 Is the assumption that the fine-detail threshold is the right legibility bar validated, or carried forward from 036 without re-examination at the new sizes? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK042 Is the assumption that pinch zoom adequately covers small viewports supported by anything beyond precedent elsewhere in the client? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]

- **2026-08-18 — reviewed against the spec; 12 items produced spec edits.**
  CHK008, CHK009, CHK010, CHK014, CHK021, CHK027, CHK029, CHK030, CHK031,
  CHK032, CHK034, CHK035, CHK036 and CHK038 are now addressed: the spec gained
  FR-011 (the minimum wins over the threshold, deliberately), FR-012 (the world

- **2026-08-18 — the amendment surface was repaired, not just found.** All ten
  `nominal` sites in 036 now carry a pointer to 037: a banner at the top, and an
  inline note at FR-003, FR-004, FR-005, FR-014, SC-001, the User Story 1

  following 004→006: 036 records what shipped, and until 037 is built its rules

- **2026-08-18 — the four decision items are all decided, so nothing here is

  constraint that follows from the construction and would need renegotiating the
  moment anything widens the range on purpose). CHK041 is answered the hard way —

  monitors, so the 44px threshold was deleted from `cat-v2.js` and `props.js`
  rather than cleared by the band. CHK039 is answered by the owner making Fog an
  **influence, not a dependency**: nothing here is conditional on it and no
  acceptance criterion waits for it.
- **2026-08-18 — the threshold's deletion was propagated.** It had been applied
  to `spec.md` only, leaving `tasks.md`, `quickstart.md`, `data-model.md`,
  `contracts/zoom.md` and `research.md` still asserting a band that clears 44px —
  including a Phase 5 sweep check that would have passed vacuously on a premise
  that no longer exists. Also withdrawn as consequences: **FR-011** (it arbitrated
  minimum-versus-threshold; with no threshold FR-006 already covers it) and the
  Assumption "the fine-detail threshold is the right legibility bar". `ceilingPx`
  now rests on `PORTRAIT_CAT = 47` alone.
